steps.instruction: Wash and dry the bike, paying attention to the steering head, clamps and fork tubes. Lay out a clean tray and zip bags with a marker; you will have a lot of bolts off at once.
steps.title: Wash and prep

steps.instruction: Put the bike on a stand under the engine so the front wheel hangs clear. Push on the bars from each side to make sure it cannot rock off. Once the forks are out the bike gets tail-heavy, so strap the rear down or weight it if your stand is narrow.
steps.title: Lift the front wheel
verification: Front wheel clear of the ground

steps.instruction: With the bars straight, grab the bottom of the fork legs and rock them forward and back, feeling for a clunk at the head. Then turn the bars slowly lock to lock and feel for notches or a spot where the steering wants to stop in the center. Write down what you find.
steps.title: Check the steering before you start

steps.instruction: Measure how far the fork tubes stand above the top clamp and write it down for both legs. Count the compression and rebound clicker positions back to the stop and note them, then return them to where they were.
steps.title: Record fork height and clickers
verification: Fork height and clicker positions written down

steps.instruction: Take out the number plate bolt and lift the plate off its tabs.
steps.title: Remove the number plate

steps.instruction: Disconnect the two warning lights mounted on the upper clamp (engine trouble and fuel level) at their connectors, and free the leads from their clips so the clamp can come off.
steps.title: Unplug the warning lights

steps.instruction: Loosen the four axle pinch bolts at the bottom of both fork legs, then crack the axle nut loose. Do not take anything off yet; the wheel is still holding the forks in line.
steps.title: Loosen the axle
verification: Pinch bolts and axle nut loose

steps.instruction: Hold the wheel, unscrew the axle nut and slide the axle out. Lower the wheel out of the forks and lay it with the disc facing up. Pick up the two collars from the hub and keep them with the axle so they go back on the correct sides.
steps.title: Pull the front wheel
verification: Wheel out, axle and both collars bagged together

steps.instruction: Remove the two front caliper bolts and slide the caliper off the disc. Free the brake hose from the guard and hose clamps on the fork leg, then hang the caliper from the frame with a strap so the hose is not stretched or kinked. Do not squeeze the brake lever while the caliper is off.
steps.title: Unbolt and hang the caliper
verification: Caliper supported, hose not under strain

steps.instruction: Undo the front fender bolts under the lower clamp and lift the fender away.
steps.title: Remove the front fender

steps.instruction: Remove the upper handlebar holder bolts and lift the bar with the controls still on it. Lay it over the tank on a rag so the master cylinder stays upright and the cables and hose are not kinked.
steps.title: Take off the handlebar
verification: Bar resting safely, master cylinder upright

steps.instruction: With the forks still in the clamps to hold everything, crack the big steering stem nut loose on top of the upper clamp. Do not remove it yet.
steps.title: Break the steering stem nut loose

steps.instruction: Support one fork leg, loosen its upper and lower clamp pinch bolts and slide the leg down out of the clamps, twisting gently if it sticks. Repeat for the other leg. Stand both legs upright and label them left and right.
steps.title: Drop the fork legs out
verification: Both legs out, labeled and upright

steps.instruction: Remove the stem nut and washer and lift the upper clamp off the stem. Set it aside with the bar holders still attached.
steps.title: Lift off the upper clamp

steps.instruction: Hold the lower clamp up with one hand so it cannot drop, then unscrew the ring nut using the hook-type steering nut wrench, then lift off the bearing race cover (the upper seal) and the upper bearing.
steps.title: Remove the ring nut
verification: Ring nut, cover and upper bearing removed

steps.instruction: Slide the lower clamp and stem down out of the head tube. The lower bearing stays on the stem.
steps.title: Lower the stem out

branches.condition: Every roller and both race surfaces are smooth with no pitting, dents or wear marks, and the clamps are straight and uncracked.
branches.label: Bearings and races are good

steps.instruction: Wash the bearings, the stem and both races in the head tube with kerosene or parts cleaner and dry them. Look at every roller and race surface: pitting, flat spots, rust, dents or a worn line where the bike usually sits straight ahead all mean replace. Also check both clamps and the stem for bends or cracks. Write down what you found.
steps.title: Clean and inspect bearings and races
verification: Bearings, races and clamps inspected and condition written down

steps.instruction: If either clamp or the stem is bent or cracked, it must be replaced with a new part before going any further. Bearings alone will not fix it.
steps.title: Stop if a clamp or the stem is damaged
verification: Clamps and stem confirmed straight, or new parts on hand

steps.instruction: Reach through the head tube with a long drift and tap the far race out a little at a time, moving the drift around the race so it walks out straight. Do the same from the other end. Clean the bores and check them for scores or cracks.
steps.title: Knock out the head tube races

steps.instruction: Lift the lower bearing and its seal off the stem by working a small chisel under the inner race, going around evenly. Take care not to gouge the stem.
steps.title: Remove the lower bearing from the stem

steps.instruction: Drive each new race into the head tube with a driver or socket that bears only on the outer edge of the race. Keep it square and go until the note of the hammer changes and the race is fully seated against its shoulder. A race that goes in crooked can damage the head tube, so stop and correct it if it starts to tilt.
steps.title: Fit the new races
verification: Both races fully seated and square

steps.instruction: Press the new lower bearing onto the stem with a tube that pushes only on the inner race, all the way down to the shoulder. Bearings and races are always fitted as matched new sets.
steps.title: Fit the new lower bearing on the stem
verification: Lower bearing seated on the stem

steps.instruction: Pack both bearings with lithium-soap grease, working it into the rollers, and coat both races. Grease the lower seal lip, the inner bore of the lower bearing, the stem threads and the band of the stem just above the lower bearing.
steps.title: Grease the bearings
verification: Seal lip and stem threads greased

steps.instruction: Push the lower clamp and stem up into the head tube and hold it there. Drop the upper bearing onto its race and fit the bearing race cover over it, with grease on the cover lip.
steps.title: Slide the stem back in
verification: Stem in, upper bearing and cover in place

steps.instruction: Screw the ring nut on with its stepped side facing down. Using the steering nut wrench, with your torque wrench held at a right angle to it, tighten the ring nut to about 38 N·m (28 lb-ft) to seat the bearings. Swing the bars from side to side a few times as it tightens.
steps.title: Seat the ring nut
verification: Ring nut taken to 38 N·m (28 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Loosen the ring nut one full turn, then tighten it again to 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft). Do not go over this; too much preload ruins new bearings quickly. Turn the stem lock to lock: it should swing freely with no binding and no play.
steps.title: Set the bearing preload
verification: Steering swings freely with no play

steps.instruction: Put the washer on, fit the upper clamp, then slide each fork leg up through both clamps to the height you recorded (stock is 5 mm of tube above the top clamp). Snug the lower clamp pinch bolts just enough to hold the legs; leave the upper pinch bolts loose for now.
steps.title: Refit the washer, upper clamp and fork legs
verification: Both legs at the same height (5 mm stock)

steps.instruction: Put a little lithium-soap grease on the contact face of the stem nut and torque it to 145 N·m (107 lb-ft).
steps.title: Torque the steering stem nut

steps.instruction: Turn the bars lock to lock again. If the steering now feels tight or catches, the ring nut is too tight: take the stem nut and upper clamp back off and ease the ring nut back a little at a time until it is free, then refit.
steps.title: Check the steering moves freely

steps.instruction: Check the fork heights are equal, then tighten the upper clamp pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft) and the lower clamp pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft). Do not go over the lower clamp torque; overtightening squeezes the fork tube and makes the fork stick.
steps.title: Tighten the clamp pinch bolts
verification: Upper pinch bolts at 21 N·m (15 lb-ft)
Lower pinch bolts at 21 N·m (15 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Set the bar back in the lower holders, fit the upper holders with their punch marks facing forward, and tighten the front bolts first and then the rear bolts to 28 N·m (21 lb-ft). The gap should end up at the back.
steps.title: Refit the handlebar

steps.instruction: Put the fender back and tighten its bolts to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the front fender

steps.instruction: Refit the brake hose to the fork guard and holders exactly as it was (hose holder bolt 9 N·m (6.6 lb-ft)), with the guard bolts at 5 N·m (3.7 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the brake hose clamps
verification: Hose routed as before, not twisted

steps.instruction: Unhook the caliper and bolt it back onto the fork leg, torquing the two caliper bolts to 28 N·m (21 lb-ft). Check the pads are seated and spread enough for the disc.
steps.title: Bolt the caliper back on

steps.instruction: Grease the axle lightly with lithium-soap grease. Fit the collars to the hub on their own sides, lift the wheel into the forks with the disc sliding between the brake pads, and push the axle through from the side it came out.
steps.title: Lift the front wheel into the forks

steps.instruction: Fit the axle nut and run it down. Before the final pull, take the bike off the stand or push hard on the bars a few times so the forks settle and slide freely on the axle. Then torque the axle nut to 115 N·m (85 lb-ft).
steps.title: Torque the axle nut

steps.instruction: Tighten the four axle pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft), going back and forth between the two bolts on each leg so the clamp closes evenly.
steps.title: Tighten the axle pinch bolts
verification: All four pinch bolts at 21 N·m (15 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Squeeze the front brake lever several times until it is firm, then spin the wheel. It should turn freely with only light pad drag and stop hard when you pull the lever.
steps.title: Pump up the front brake
verification: Wheel spins freely and brakes properly

steps.instruction: Hook the number plate on and tighten its bolt to 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the number plate
verification: Number plate bolt at 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Plug both warning-light leads back in and clip them where they were.
steps.title: Reconnect the warning lights

steps.instruction: Set the clickers back to your recorded positions. Off the stand, hold the front brake and rock the bike back and forth; there must be no clunk at the head. Turn the bars lock to lock with the wheel off the ground; they should fall to each side smoothly. Check the cables and hoses do not pull at full lock.
steps.title: Final steering check
verification: No play at the steering head
Cables and hoses free at full lock

title: Service or replace the steering head bearings

completeness: Removes the rear wheel, linkage and swingarm, replaces the linkage needle bearings, collars and seals and the swingarm pivot bearings, bushings and seals as needed, sets the installed depths, then refits everything with the chain riveted and slack set; the shock itself is not opened.
critical_stop_conditions: Pivot shaft or any linkage bolt bent: replace, never straighten.
Needle bearing bore oversize, cracked or the new bearing goes in loose: replace the arm or swingarm.
Swingarm cracked or bent: replace it.
Linkage binds after assembly: stop and find the cause before riding.
Riveted master link outside its measurement window: cut it off and fit another new link.
entry_state: Complete bike, cold, on a stand under the engine with the rear wheel clear.
excluded: Shock internal service or shock eye bearings (see the shock guide)
Chain or sprocket replacement beyond fitting a new master link
exit_state: Linkage and swingarm pivot bearings renewed and greased, swingarm, linkage, shock, rear brake, wheel and chain refitted and torqued, chain slack set; rear suspension moves freely; ready to ride.
prerequisites: Bike washed underneath, especially the linkage and swingarm pivot.
Engine support ready: the swingarm pivot shaft also carries the back of the engine.

required_parts.name: Linkage: 6 needle bearings, 3 collars, 6 oil seals (inspect the 8 washers)
required_parts.purpose: Bearings and collars are replaced as sets; seals are always new

required_parts.name: Swingarm pivot: 4 needle bearings, 2 bushings, 2 thrust bearings, 4 oil seals, inspect 2 collars
required_parts.purpose: Bearings and bushings are replaced as sets; seals are always new

required_parts.name: New drive chain master link
required_parts.purpose: The chain is riveted; the link removed to split it cannot be reused

required_tools.name: Maintenance stand plus a jack or block to support the engine
Needle bearing press tool or threaded rod with sockets and washers
A spare shaft or long bolt the diameter of the pivot shaft

steps.instruction: Pressure-wash the underside of the bike away from the bearing seals and let it dry. Grit in the linkage is the reason most of these bearings fail. Lay out labeled bags for each joint.
steps.title: Wash and prep

steps.instruction: Put the bike on a stand under the engine with the rear wheel clear. Have a jack or block ready under the engine as well; once the pivot shaft comes out the engine hangs on its other mounts only.
steps.title: Lift and support the bike

steps.instruction: With the wheel off the ground, lift the back of the tire and feel for clunks in the linkage. Then grab the back of the swingarm and push it side to side to feel for pivot play. Note what you find.
steps.title: Check for play before you start

steps.instruction: Find the master link and cut the chain there with a chain cut-and-rivet tool. Lay the chain over the sprocket so it does not fall into the dirt.
steps.title: Split the chain
verification: Chain split at the master link

steps.instruction: Remove the rear axle nut, slide the axle out and lower the wheel out of the swingarm. Keep the collars and both chain pullers labeled. Do not press the brake pedal from here on.
steps.title: Pull the rear wheel
verification: Wheel out, collars and pullers bagged

steps.instruction: Slide the rear caliper bracket off the swingarm slide rail, unscrew the brake hose holders from the swingarm and tie the caliper up to the frame without kinking the hose.
steps.title: Free the rear caliper and hose

steps.instruction: Support the swingarm with one hand and pull the shock lower bolt out so the swingarm does not drop.
steps.title: Undo the shock lower bolt
verification: Shock lower bolt out, swingarm supported

steps.instruction: Remove the connecting arm bolt at the frame, the relay arm bolt at the swingarm and the bolt joining the two arms. Note which side each bolt went in from. Lift both arms out together and keep all washers and collars with them.
steps.title: Remove the relay arm and connecting arm

steps.instruction: Put the jack or block under the engine and take its weight lightly, so nothing shifts when the pivot shaft comes out.
steps.title: Support the engine

steps.instruction: Remove the pivot shaft nut and drive the shaft out with a brass drift while you hold the swingarm. Slide a spare shaft in behind it from the other side if you can, so the engine stays aligned. Lift the swingarm out to the rear.
steps.title: Pull the pivot shaft and swingarm

steps.instruction: Clean the pivot shaft in kerosene and roll it on a flat surface; any rock means it is bent and must be replaced. Look the swingarm over for cracks and bends.
steps.title: Check the pivot shaft and swingarm

steps.instruction: Drive each new race into the head tube with a driver or socket that bears only on the outer edge of the race. Keep it square and go until the note of the hammer changes and the race is fully seated against its shoulder. A race that goes in crooked can damage the head tube, so stop and correct it if it starts to tilt.
steps.title: Fit the new races
verification: Both races fully seated and square

steps.instruction: Press the new lower bearing onto the stem with a tube that pushes only on the inner race, all the way down to the shoulder. Bearings and races are always fitted as matched new sets.
steps.title: Fit the new lower bearing on the stem
verification: Lower bearing seated on the stem

steps.instruction: Pack both bearings with lithium-soap grease, working it into the rollers, and coat both races. Grease the lower seal lip, the inner bore of the lower bearing, the stem threads and the band of the stem just above the lower bearing.
steps.title: Grease the bearings
verification: Seal lip and stem threads greased

steps.instruction: Push the lower clamp and stem up into the head tube and hold it there. Drop the upper bearing onto its race and fit the bearing race cover over it, with grease on the cover lip.
steps.title: Slide the stem back in
verification: Stem in, upper bearing and cover in place

steps.instruction: Screw the ring nut on with its stepped side facing down. Using the steering nut wrench, with your torque wrench held at a right angle to it, tighten the ring nut to about 38 N·m (28 lb-ft) to seat the bearings. Swing the bars from side to side a few times as it tightens.
steps.title: Seat the ring nut
verification: Ring nut taken to 38 N·m (28 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Loosen the ring nut one full turn, then tighten it again to 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft). Do not go over this; too much preload ruins new bearings quickly. Turn the stem lock to lock: it should swing freely with no binding and no play.
steps.title: Set the bearing preload
verification: Steering swings freely with no play

steps.instruction: Put the washer on, fit the upper clamp, then slide each fork leg up through both clamps to the height you recorded (stock is 5 mm of tube above the top clamp). Snug the lower clamp pinch bolts just enough to hold the legs; leave the upper pinch bolts loose for now.
steps.title: Refit the washer, upper clamp and fork legs
verification: Both legs at the same height (5 mm stock)

steps.instruction: Put a little lithium-soap grease on the contact face of the stem nut and torque it to 145 N·m (107 lb-ft).
steps.title: Torque the steering stem nut

steps.instruction: Turn the bars lock to lock again. If the steering now feels tight or catches, the ring nut is too tight: take the stem nut and upper clamp back off and ease the ring nut back a little at a time until it is free, then refit.
steps.title: Check the steering moves freely

steps.instruction: Check the fork heights are equal, then tighten the upper clamp pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft) and the lower clamp pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft). Do not go over the lower clamp torque; overtightening squeezes the fork tube and makes the fork stick.
steps.title: Tighten the clamp pinch bolts
verification: Upper pinch bolts at 21 N·m (15 lb-ft)
Lower pinch bolts at 21 N·m (15 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Set the bar back in the lower holders, fit the upper holders with their punch marks facing forward, and tighten the front bolts first and then the rear bolts to 28 N·m (21 lb-ft). The gap should end up at the back.
steps.title: Refit the handlebar

steps.instruction: Put the fender back and tighten its bolts to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the front fender

steps.instruction: Refit the brake hose to the fork guard and holders exactly as it was, with the guard bolts at 5 N·m (3.7 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the brake hose clamps
verification: Hose routed as before, not twisted

steps.instruction: Unhook the caliper and bolt it back onto the fork leg, torquing the two caliper bolts to 28 N·m (21 lb-ft). Check the pads are seated and spread enough for the disc.
steps.title: Bolt the caliper back on

steps.instruction: Grease the axle lightly with lithium-soap grease. Fit the collars to the hub on their own sides, lift the wheel into the forks with the disc sliding between the brake pads, and push the axle through from the side it came out.
steps.title: Lift the front wheel into the forks

steps.instruction: Put the speed sensor back on the left leg with its bracket, keeping the lead in its original routing. Tighten the bolt to 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft). Check nothing magnetic or metallic is stuck to the sensor face.
steps.title: Refit the speed sensor

steps.instruction: Fit the axle nut and run it down. Before the final pull, take the bike off the stand or push hard on the bars a few times so the forks settle and slide freely on the axle. Then torque the axle nut to 115 N·m (85 lb-ft).
steps.title: Torque the axle nut

steps.instruction: Tighten the four axle pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft), going back and forth between the two bolts on each leg so the clamp closes evenly.
steps.title: Tighten the axle pinch bolts
verification: All four pinch bolts at 21 N·m (15 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Squeeze the front brake lever several times until it is firm, then spin the wheel. It should turn freely with only light pad drag and stop hard when you pull the lever.
steps.title: Pump up the front brake
verification: Wheel spins freely and brakes properly

steps.instruction: Refit the meter bracket (7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft)) and the headlight body (7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft)), plug in all the couplers, and check the headlight and meter work.
steps.title: Refit the meter and headlight

steps.instruction: Set the clickers back to your recorded positions. Off the stand, hold the front brake and rock the bike back and forth; there must be no clunk at the head. Turn the bars lock to lock with the wheel off the ground; they should fall to each side smoothly. Check the cables and hoses do not pull at full lock.
steps.title: Final steering check
verification: No play at the steering head
Cables and hoses free at full lock

title: Service or replace the steering head bearings

completeness: Takes the front wheel, fork legs, handlebar and both triple clamps off, then either cleans and regreases the steering head bearings or replaces both bearings and races, sets the bearing preload and rebuilds to a ready-to-ride front end; fork internals are not opened.
critical_stop_conditions: Bearing race bore in the head tube scored, cracked or loose on a new race: stop, this is frame repair.
New bearings still notchy after assembly: stop and recheck that both races are fully seated before riding.
Any front-to-back play at the steering head after adjustment: do not ride.
Steering binds after the stem nut is torqued: back the ring nut off slightly and recheck; never ride with tight steering.
Brake hose kinked or stretched while the caliper hangs: inspect it and replace if damaged.
entry_state: Complete bike, cold, on a stand under the engine.
excluded: Frame repair or a damaged head tube bore
exit_state: Steering head bearings regreased or renewed, ring nut preload set, clamps, fork legs, handlebar, fender and front wheel refitted and torqued, steering free of play and binding; ready to ride.
prerequisites: Bike washed, especially around the steering head and clamps.
Note the fork leg height in the clamps and your clicker settings before you start.

required_parts.name: Upper and lower steering head bearings with their races
required_parts.purpose: Only if inspection shows damage or pitting; bearings and races are always replaced as a set

required_parts.name: Bearing race cover (upper dust seal)
required_parts.purpose: Replace if torn or hardened when the bearings are renewed

required_tools.name: Maintenance stand that lifts the front wheel clear
Steering nut wrench (hook wrench) that fits the ring nut and accepts a torque wrench at a right angle
Long brass or steel drift for knocking out the head tube races
Small chisel for lifting the lower race off the stem
Bearing race driver or a socket matched to each race outer diameter
Sockets and hex bits for the clamp, axle and caliper fasteners
Parts washer or kerosene and clean rags

steps.instruction: Wash and dry the bike, paying attention to the steering head, clamps and fork tubes. Lay out a clean tray and zip bags with a marker; you will have a lot of bolts off at once.
steps.title: Wash and prep

steps.instruction: Put the bike on a stand under the engine so the front wheel hangs clear. Push on the bars from each side to make sure it cannot rock off. Once the forks are out the bike gets tail-heavy, so strap the rear down or weight it if your stand is narrow.
steps.title: Lift the front wheel
verification: Front wheel clear of the ground

steps.instruction: With the bars straight, grab the bottom of the fork legs and rock them forward and back, feeling for a clunk at the head. Then turn the bars slowly lock to lock and feel for notches or a spot where the steering wants to stop in the center. Write down what you find.
steps.title: Check the steering before you start

steps.instruction: Measure how far the fork tubes stand above the top clamp and write it down for both legs. Count the compression and rebound clicker positions back to the stop and note them, then return them to where they were.
steps.title: Record fork height and clickers
verification: Fork height and clicker positions written down

steps.instruction: Unplug the headlight, speed sensor and meter couplers, then take off the headlight body and the meter with its bracket. Photograph the wiring and cable routing first. Bag the fasteners together.
steps.title: Remove the headlight and meter

steps.instruction: Undo the speed sensor bracket bolt on the left fork leg and lift the sensor away from the wheel without pulling on its lead. Tape it to the fork guard so it hangs clear. Keep magnetic tools away from the sensor and its rotor on the wheel.
steps.title: Unbolt the speed sensor
verification: Sensor hanging free, lead not stretched

steps.instruction: Loosen the four axle pinch bolts at the bottom of both fork legs, then crack the axle nut loose. Do not take anything off yet; the wheel is still holding the forks in line.
steps.title: Loosen the axle
verification: Pinch bolts and axle nut loose

steps.instruction: Hold the wheel, unscrew the axle nut and slide the axle out. Lower the wheel out of the forks and lay it with the disc facing up. Pick up the two collars from the hub and keep them with the axle so they go back on the correct sides.
steps.title: Pull the front wheel
verification: Wheel out, axle and both collars bagged together

steps.instruction: Remove the two front caliper bolts and slide the caliper off the disc. Free the brake hose from the guard and hose clamps on the fork leg, then hang the caliper from the frame with a strap so the hose is not stretched or kinked. Do not squeeze the brake lever while the caliper is off.
steps.title: Unbolt and hang the caliper
verification: Caliper supported, hose not under strain

steps.instruction: Undo the front fender bolts under the lower clamp and lift the fender away.
steps.title: Remove the front fender

steps.instruction: Remove the upper handlebar holder bolts and lift the bar with the controls still on it. Lay it over the tank on a rag so the master cylinder stays upright and the cables and hose are not kinked.
steps.title: Take off the handlebar
verification: Bar resting safely, master cylinder upright

steps.instruction: With the forks still in the clamps to hold everything, crack the big steering stem nut loose on top of the upper clamp. Do not remove it yet.
steps.title: Break the steering stem nut loose

steps.instruction: Support one fork leg, loosen its upper and lower clamp pinch bolts and slide the leg down out of the clamps, twisting gently if it sticks. Repeat for the other leg. Stand both legs upright and label them left and right.
steps.title: Drop the fork legs out
verification: Both legs out, labeled and upright

steps.instruction: Remove the stem nut and washer and lift the upper clamp off the stem. Set it aside with the bar holders still attached.
steps.title: Lift off the upper clamp

steps.instruction: Hold the lower clamp up with one hand so it cannot drop, then unscrew the ring nut using the hook-type steering nut wrench, then lift off the bearing race cover (the upper seal) and the upper bearing.
steps.title: Remove the ring nut
verification: Ring nut, cover and upper bearing removed

steps.instruction: Slide the lower clamp and stem down out of the head tube. The lower bearing stays on the stem.
steps.title: Lower the stem out

branches.condition: Every roller and both race surfaces are smooth with no pitting, dents or wear marks, and the clamps are straight and uncracked.
branches.label: Bearings and races are good

steps.instruction: Wash the bearings, the stem and both races in the head tube with kerosene or parts cleaner and dry them. Look at every roller and race surface: pitting, flat spots, rust, dents or a worn line where the bike usually sits straight ahead all mean replace. Also check both clamps and the stem for bends or cracks. Write down what you found.
steps.title: Clean and inspect bearings and races
verification: Bearings, races and clamps inspected and condition written down

steps.instruction: If either clamp or the stem is bent or cracked, it must be replaced with a new part before going any further. Bearings alone will not fix it.
steps.title: Stop if a clamp or the stem is damaged
verification: Clamps and stem confirmed straight, or new parts on hand

steps.instruction: Reach through the head tube with a long drift and tap the far race out a little at a time, moving the drift around the race so it walks out straight. Do the same from the other end. Clean the bores and check them for scores or cracks.
steps.title: Knock out the head tube races

steps.instruction: Lift the lower bearing and its seal off the stem by working a small chisel under the inner race, going around evenly. Take care not to gouge the stem.
steps.title: Remove the lower bearing from the stem

steps.instruction: Drive each new race into the head tube with a driver or socket that bears only on the outer edge of the race. Keep it square and go until the note of the hammer changes and the race is fully seated against its shoulder. A race that goes in crooked can damage the head tube, so stop and correct it if it starts to tilt.
steps.title: Fit the new races
verification: Both races fully seated and square

steps.instruction: Press the new lower bearing onto the stem with a tube that pushes only on the inner race, all the way down to the shoulder. Bearings and races are always fitted as matched new sets.
steps.title: Fit the new lower bearing on the stem
verification: Lower bearing seated on the stem

steps.instruction: Pack both bearings with lithium-soap grease, working it into the rollers, and coat both races. Grease the lower seal lip, the inner bore of the lower bearing, the stem threads and the band of the stem just above the lower bearing.
steps.title: Grease the bearings
verification: Seal lip and stem threads greased

steps.instruction: Push the lower clamp and stem up into the head tube and hold it there. Drop the upper bearing onto its race and fit the bearing race cover over it, with grease on the cover lip.
steps.title: Slide the stem back in
verification: Stem in, upper bearing and cover in place

steps.instruction: Screw the ring nut on with its stepped side facing down. Using the steering nut wrench, with your torque wrench held at a right angle to it, tighten the ring nut to about 38 N·m (28 lb-ft) to seat the bearings. Swing the bars from side to side a few times as it tightens.
steps.title: Seat the ring nut
verification: Ring nut taken to 38 N·m (28 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Loosen the ring nut one full turn, then tighten it again to 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft). Do not go over this; too much preload ruins new bearings quickly. Turn the stem lock to lock: it should swing freely with no binding and no play.
steps.title: Set the bearing preload
verification: Steering swings freely with no play

steps.instruction: Put the washer on, fit the upper clamp, then slide each fork leg up through both clamps to the height you recorded (stock is 8 mm of tube above the top clamp). Snug the lower clamp pinch bolts just enough to hold the legs; leave the upper pinch bolts loose for now.
steps.title: Refit the washer, upper clamp and fork legs
verification: Both legs at the same height (8 mm stock)

steps.instruction: Put a little lithium-soap grease on the contact face of the stem nut and torque it to 145 N·m (107 lb-ft).
steps.title: Torque the steering stem nut

steps.instruction: Turn the bars lock to lock again. If the steering now feels tight or catches, the ring nut is too tight: take the stem nut and upper clamp back off and ease the ring nut back a little at a time until it is free, then refit.
steps.title: Check the steering moves freely

steps.instruction: Check the fork heights are equal, then tighten the upper clamp pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft) and the lower clamp pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft). Do not go over the lower clamp torque; overtightening squeezes the fork tube and makes the fork stick.
steps.title: Tighten the clamp pinch bolts
verification: Upper pinch bolts at 21 N·m (15 lb-ft)
Lower pinch bolts at 21 N·m (15 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Set the bar back in the lower holders, fit the upper holders with their punch marks facing forward, and tighten the front bolts first and then the rear bolts to 28 N·m (21 lb-ft). The gap should end up at the back.
steps.title: Refit the handlebar

steps.instruction: Put the fender back and tighten its bolts to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the front fender

steps.instruction: Refit the brake hose to the fork guard and holders exactly as it was, with the guard bolts at 5 N·m (3.7 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the brake hose clamps
verification: Hose routed as before, not twisted

steps.instruction: Unhook the caliper and bolt it back onto the fork leg, torquing the two caliper bolts to 28 N·m (21 lb-ft). Check the pads are seated and spread enough for the disc.
steps.title: Bolt the caliper back on

steps.instruction: Grease the axle lightly with lithium-soap grease. Fit the collars to the hub on their own sides, lift the wheel into the forks with the disc sliding between the brake pads, and push the axle through from the side it came out.
steps.title: Lift the front wheel into the forks

steps.instruction: Put the speed sensor back on the left leg with its bracket, keeping the lead in its original routing. Tighten the bolt to 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft). Check nothing magnetic or metallic is stuck to the sensor face.
steps.title: Refit the speed sensor

steps.instruction: Fit the axle nut and run it down. Before the final pull, take the bike off the stand or push hard on the bars a few times so the forks settle and slide freely on the axle. Then torque the axle nut to 115 N·m (85 lb-ft).
steps.title: Torque the axle nut

steps.instruction: Tighten the four axle pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft), going back and forth between the two bolts on each leg so the clamp closes evenly.
steps.title: Tighten the axle pinch bolts
verification: All four pinch bolts at 21 N·m (15 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Squeeze the front brake lever several times until it is firm, then spin the wheel. It should turn freely with only light pad drag and stop hard when you pull the lever.
steps.title: Pump up the front brake
verification: Wheel spins freely and brakes properly

steps.instruction: Refit the meter bracket (7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft)) and the headlight body (7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft)), plug in all the couplers, and check the headlight and meter work.
steps.title: Refit the meter and headlight

steps.instruction: Set the clickers back to your recorded positions. Off the stand, hold the front brake and rock the bike back and forth; there must be no clunk at the head. Turn the bars lock to lock with the wheel off the ground; they should fall to each side smoothly. Check the cables and hoses do not pull at full lock.
steps.title: Final steering check
verification: No play at the steering head
Cables and hoses free at full lock

title: Service or replace the steering head bearings

completeness: Removes the rear wheel, linkage and swingarm, replaces the linkage needle bearings, collars and seals and the swingarm pivot bearings, bushings and seals as needed, sets the installed depths, then refits everything with the chain riveted and slack set; the shock itself is not opened.
critical_stop_conditions: Pivot shaft or any linkage bolt bent: replace, never straighten.
Needle bearing bore oversize, cracked or the new bearing goes in loose: replace the arm or swingarm.
Swingarm cracked or bent: replace it.
Linkage binds after assembly: stop and find the cause before riding.
Riveted master link outside its measurement window: cut it off and fit another new link.
entry_state: Complete bike, cold, on a stand under the engine with the rear wheel clear.
excluded: Shock internal service or shock eye bearings (see the shock guide)
Chain or sprocket replacement beyond fitting a new master link
exit_state: Linkage and swingarm pivot bearings renewed and greased, swingarm, linkage, shock, rear brake, wheel and chain refitted and torqued, chain slack set; rear suspension moves freely; ready to ride.
prerequisites: Bike washed underneath, especially the linkage and swingarm pivot.
Engine support ready: the swingarm pivot shaft also carries the back of the engine.

required_parts.name: Linkage: 6 needle bearings, 3 collars, 6 oil seals (inspect the 8 washers)
required_parts.purpose: Bearings and collars are replaced as sets; seals are always new

required_parts.name: Swingarm pivot: 4 needle bearings, 2 bushings, 2 thrust bearings, 4 oil seals, inspect 2 collars
required_parts.purpose: Bearings and bushings are replaced as sets; seals are always new

required_parts.name: New drive chain master link
required_parts.purpose: The chain is riveted; the link removed to split it cannot be reused

required_tools.name: Maintenance stand plus a jack or block to support the engine
Needle bearing press tool or threaded rod with sockets and washers
A spare shaft or long bolt the diameter of the pivot shaft

steps.instruction: Pressure-wash the underside of the bike away from the bearing seals and let it dry. Grit in the linkage is the reason most of these bearings fail. Lay out labeled bags for each joint.
steps.title: Wash and prep

steps.instruction: Put the bike on a stand under the engine with the rear wheel clear. Have a jack or block ready under the engine as well; once the pivot shaft comes out the engine hangs on its other mounts only.
steps.title: Lift and support the bike

steps.instruction: With the wheel off the ground, lift the back of the tire and feel for clunks in the linkage. Then grab the back of the swingarm and push it side to side to feel for pivot play. Note what you find.
steps.title: Check for play before you start

steps.instruction: Find the master link and cut the chain there with a chain cut-and-rivet tool. Lay the chain over the sprocket so it does not fall into the dirt.
steps.title: Split the chain
verification: Chain split at the master link

steps.instruction: Remove the rear axle nut, slide the axle out and lower the wheel out of the swingarm. Keep the collars and both chain pullers labeled. Do not press the brake pedal from here on.
steps.title: Pull the rear wheel
verification: Wheel out, collars and pullers bagged

steps.instruction: Slide the rear caliper bracket off the swingarm slide rail, unscrew the brake hose holders from the swingarm and tie the caliper up to the frame without kinking the hose.
steps.title: Free the rear caliper and hose

steps.instruction: Support the swingarm with one hand and pull the shock lower bolt out so the swingarm does not drop.
steps.title: Undo the shock lower bolt
verification: Shock lower bolt out, swingarm supported

steps.instruction: Remove the connecting arm bolt at the frame, the relay arm bolt at the swingarm and the bolt joining the two arms. Note which side each bolt went in from. Lift both arms out together and keep all washers and collars with them.
steps.title: Remove the relay arm and connecting arm

steps.instruction: Put the jack or block under the engine and take its weight lightly, so nothing shifts when the pivot shaft comes out.
steps.title: Support the engine

steps.instruction: Remove the pivot shaft nut and drive the shaft out with a brass drift while you hold the swingarm. Slide a spare shaft in behind it from the other side if you can, so the engine stays aligned. Lift the swingarm out to the rear.
steps.title: Pull the pivot shaft and swingarm

steps.instruction: Clean the pivot shaft in kerosene and roll it on a flat surface; any rock means it is bent and must be replaced. Look the swingarm over for cracks and bends.
steps.title: Check the pivot shaft and swingarm

branches.condition: Needle bearings and bushings turn smoothly with no play or rust and the collars are not pitted; only the seals will be renewed.
branches.label: Pivot bearings are good

steps.instruction: Pull out the collars, seals and thrust bearings. Clean the needle bearings and bushings and check them for play, rough rotation and rust, and the collars for pitting. Write down the condition.
steps.title: Inspect the swingarm pivot bearings
verification: Pivot bearings, bushings and collars inspected

steps.instruction: Press the four needle bearings out of the swingarm pivot with a bearing press or a threaded rod with sockets and washers. Pull the bushings at the same time; bearings and bushings are replaced as a set. Clean the bores.
steps.title: Press out the swingarm bearings
verification: All swingarm bearings and bushings out

steps.instruction: Grease the new needle bearings with molybdenum disulfide grease. On each side of the pivot, press the outer bearing in first and then the inner one, pushing from the inside of the swingarm. The inner bearing on each side finishes 6.5 mm in from the inner end of the pivot boss. Measure each depth and write it down. The new seals that go in later sit 0–0.5 mm below the outer faces.
steps.title: Press in the new swingarm bearings
verification: Bearings pressed from the inside, outer first
Inner bearing depth 6.5 mm on both sides

branches.condition: All linkage needle bearings turn smoothly with no play or rust and no collar is pitted or scratched; only the seals will be renewed.
branches.label: Linkage bearings are good

steps.instruction: Between them the relay arm and connecting arm hold six needle bearings, three collars, six oil seals and eight washers. Pull the collars and seals out, clean the bearings and check each for rough spots, play or rust, and each collar for pitting or scratches. Write down the condition.
steps.title: Inspect the linkage bearings
verification: Every linkage joint inspected and recorded

steps.instruction: Press the needle bearings out of the relay arm and connecting arm one joint at a time. Bearings and their collars are replaced as sets. Clean the bores and check them for damage.
steps.title: Press out the linkage bearings

steps.instruction: Grease the new bearings with molybdenum disulfide grease and press each one in square, finishing 0 mm from the bore face (flush). Measure and note each one.
steps.title: Press in the new linkage bearings

steps.instruction: Grease all bearings, washers, collars, bushings and the thrust bearings with molybdenum disulfide grease. Fit new oil seals to every joint of the swingarm, relay arm and connecting arm; the swingarm pivot seals sit 0–0.5 mm below the outer face. Put the washers back in their places and push the collars in.
steps.title: Grease and assemble every joint
verification: New seals in every joint at the right depth

steps.instruction: Lift the swingarm into place and push the pivot shaft through from the right side, pushing out the spare shaft if you used one. Grease the shaft with molybdenum disulfide grease and the nut threads and face with lithium-soap grease. Torque the pivot shaft nut to 85 N·m (63 lb-ft), then remove the engine support.
steps.title: Refit the swingarm
verification: Pivot shaft in from the right

steps.instruction: Swing the swingarm up and down; it should move smoothly with no binding, and there should be no side play.
steps.title: Check the swingarm moves freely

steps.instruction: Coat the shanks and threads of the connecting arm-to-frame bolt, the relay arm-to-connecting arm bolt, the relay arm-to-swingarm bolt and both shock bolts with molybdenum disulfide grease.
steps.title: Grease the linkage bolts
verification: All linkage and shock bolts greased

steps.instruction: Lift the swingarm and fit the relay arm and connecting arm. The connecting arm bolt at the frame goes in from the right; the shock lower bolt, the connecting arm-to-relay arm bolt and the relay arm-to-swingarm bolt go in from the left. Fit all nuts finger tight.
steps.title: Refit the linkage and shock lower bolt
verification: All bolts in from the correct sides

steps.instruction: Torque the connecting arm nut at the frame to 80 N·m (59 lb-ft), the connecting arm nut at the relay arm to 80 N·m (59 lb-ft), the relay arm nut at the swingarm to 70 N·m (52 lb-ft) and the shock lower nut to 53 N·m (39 lb-ft). Check the shock upper nut is at 56 N·m (41 lb-ft).
steps.title: Torque the linkage
verification: Connecting arm nuts at 80 N·m (59 lb-ft) / 80 N·m (59 lb-ft)
Relay arm nut at 70 N·m (52 lb-ft)
Shock lower nut at 53 N·m (39 lb-ft)
Shock upper nut checked at 56 N·m (41 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Slide the caliper bracket back onto the swingarm rail and screw the brake hose holders back on at 3.5 N·m (2.6 lb-ft), routing the hose as it was.
steps.title: Refit the rear caliper

steps.instruction: Fit the left chain puller, grease the axle, lift the wheel in with the disc between the pads and push the axle in from the left. Fit the right puller, washer and nut finger tight.
steps.title: Refit the rear wheel
verification: Wheel in, axle from the left

steps.instruction: Join the chain with a new master link using the cut-and-rivet tool. Press the side plate on until the gap between the pin end and the plate is 1.2–1.4 mm, then rivet the pins until each pin head spreads to 5.5–5.8 mm across. Check the inside width of the joined link is 12.1–12.3 mm. Wear eye protection.
steps.title: Rivet a new master link

steps.instruction: With the bike on the stand, set the slack to 50.0–60.0 mm using both adjusters equally, torque the axle nut to 125 N·m (92 lb-ft) and the adjuster locknuts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft). Recheck the slack.
steps.title: Set the chain slack and torque the axle

steps.instruction: Press the pedal until firm and check the wheel spins freely and stops hard.
steps.title: Pump up the rear brake

steps.instruction: Off the stand, push down hard on the seat several times. The rear should compress and rebound smoothly with no knock or squeak from the linkage. Recheck the linkage and pivot nuts after the first ride.
steps.title: Final suspension check

title: Rebuild the rear linkage and swingarm pivot bearings

completeness: Removes the rear wheel, linkage and swingarm, replaces the linkage needle bearings, collars and seals and the swingarm pivot bearings, bushings and seals as needed, sets the installed depths, then refits everything with the chain riveted and slack set; the shock itself is not opened.
critical_stop_conditions: Pivot shaft or any linkage bolt bent: replace, never straighten.

steps.instruction: Wash the bike and both hubs. Lay out bags and a marker; the left and right collars, the chain adjusters and the bearings all need to stay identified.

steps.instruction: Put the bike on a stand under the engine so both wheels can be lifted clear. Make sure it is stable before pulling on anything.
steps.title: Get the bike on the stand

steps.instruction: Spin each wheel and feel for roughness, then rock it side to side to feel for play. Write down what you find for front and rear.
steps.title: Check the bearings
verification: Front and rear bearing condition noted

steps.instruction: Undo the speed sensor bracket bolt on the left fork leg and lift the sensor away from the wheel without pulling on its lead. Tape it to the fork guard so it hangs clear. Keep magnetic tools away from the sensor and its rotor on the wheel.

verification: Sensor hanging free, lead not stretched

steps.instruction: Loosen the four axle pinch bolts at the bottom of both fork legs, then crack the axle nut loose. Do not take anything off yet; the wheel is still holding the forks in line.
steps.title: Loosen the axle
verification: Pinch bolts and axle nut loose

steps.instruction: Hold the wheel, unscrew the axle nut and slide the axle out. Lower the wheel out of the forks and lay it with the disc facing up. Pick up the two collars from the hub and keep them with the axle so they go back on the correct sides.
steps.title: Pull the front wheel
verification: Wheel out, axle and both collars bagged together

steps.instruction: Remove the rear axle nut. Loosen the chain adjuster locknuts and turn the adjusting bolts in so the wheel can move forward.

steps.instruction: Push the wheel forward and lift the chain off the sprocket. Hold the wheel, slide the axle out and lower the wheel out of the swingarm, guiding the disc out of the caliper. Keep both collars and the left and right chain pullers bagged and labeled. Do not press the rear brake pedal while the wheel is out.
steps.title: Pull the rear wheel

steps.instruction: Roll each axle on a flat surface and look for any rocking that shows a bend. Check the collars for wear steps or damage. A bent axle is replaced, not straightened.
steps.title: Check the axles and collars

steps.instruction: Put each wheel on a truing stand with a dial gauge and spin it slowly. Radial and lateral runout must both be no more than 2.0 mm and 2.0 mm. Note the readings. If spokes are loose, tighten them to the spoke torque first and measure again.
steps.title: Check wheel runout
verification: Radial runout at or under 2.0 mm
Lateral runout at or under 2.0 mm

steps.instruction: Clean the outside of the front hub. Lever both seals out with a flat screwdriver, with a folded rag under the blade so you do not mark the hub. These seals are not reused.
steps.title: Pry out the front seals

steps.instruction: Remove both front bearings with a bearing puller (or drive each one out from the other side by shifting the center spacer and tapping around the inner race). Keep the center spacer. Clean the hub bores and look for scoring or cracks.

steps.instruction: Press the new left-side bearing in first, then drop the spacer in and press in the right-side bearing. Use a socket that bears only on the outer race and keep the bearing square as it goes in; stop when it seats.

steps.instruction: Grease the lips of two new seals with lithium-soap grease and drive them in with the maker's marks facing out, to the depth they came out at. Use a socket that matches the seal outer diameter.

steps.instruction: Clean the rear hub and lever both seals out with a flat screwdriver over a rag, same as the front.
steps.title: Pry out the rear seals

steps.instruction: Remove the circlip on the brake-disc side with circlip pliers, then pull all 2 rear bearings and the center spacer. Clean the bores and check them for scoring or cracks.
steps.title: Pull the rear bearings

steps.instruction: Press the new right-side (brake disc side) bearing in first and fit a new circlip in its groove. Then drop in the spacer and press in the left-side (sprocket side) bearing. Push only on the outer race and keep each bearing square.
steps.title: Fit the new rear bearings
verification: New circlip fully in its groove

steps.instruction: Grease the lips of two new seals and drive them in with the marks facing out, to the depth they came out at.

steps.title: Check disc and sprocket fasteners
verification: Disc and sprocket fasteners at spec

steps.instruction: Push a finger through each new bearing and turn it: it should be smooth with no notch. Grease the seal lips again and fit the collars on their correct sides.
steps.title: Spin-test both hubs
verification: Collars fitted on the right sides

steps.instruction: Grease the axle lightly with lithium-soap grease. Fit the collars to the hub on their own sides, lift the wheel into the forks with the disc sliding between the brake pads, and push the axle through from the side it came out.

steps.instruction: Put the speed sensor back on the left leg with its bracket, keeping the lead in its original routing. Tighten the bolt to 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft). Check nothing magnetic or metallic is stuck to the sensor face.

steps.instruction: Fit the axle nut and run it down. Before the final pull, take the bike off the stand or push hard on the bars a few times so the forks settle and slide freely on the axle. Then torque the axle nut to 115 N·m (85 lb-ft).

steps.instruction: Tighten the four axle pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft), going back and forth between the two bolts on each leg so the clamp closes evenly.
steps.title: Tighten the axle pinch bolts
verification: All four pinch bolts at 21 N·m (15 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Squeeze the front brake lever several times until it is firm, then spin the wheel. It should turn freely with only light pad drag and stop hard when you pull the lever.
steps.title: Pump up the front brake
verification: Wheel spins freely and brakes properly

steps.instruction: If the caliper was disturbed, confirm its two bolts are at 28 N·m (21 lb-ft).

Lift the wheel into the swingarm with the disc going between the rear pads, push the wheel forward and loop the chain on the sprocket, then push the axle through from the left side. Fit the right puller, washer and axle nut finger tight.
steps.title: Lift the rear wheel in

steps.instruction: With the bike on the stand, set the chain slack to 50.0–60.0 mm by turning both adjusting bolts the same amount so the marks match on each side. Measure and record the slack.
steps.title: Set the chain slack

steps.instruction: Torque the rear axle nut to 125 N·m (92 lb-ft), then tighten both adjuster locknuts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft). Recheck the slack.
steps.title: Torque the rear axle

steps.instruction: Press the rear brake pedal until it is firm. Spin the wheel: it should turn freely and stop hard with the pedal.
steps.title: Pump up the rear brake

steps.instruction: Spin both wheels and check for wobble and noise. Off the stand, push the bike and use both brakes. Recheck the axle nuts after the first ride.
steps.title: Final check

required_parts.purpose: Always fitted new once removed

required_parts.name: Rear wheel bearings (3), seals (2) and circlip
required_parts.purpose: Always fitted new once removed

required_tools.name: Bearing puller (blind-hole type with slide hammer) or a long drift

Dial gauge and wheel stand for runout

steps.instruction: Wash the bike and both hubs. Lay out bags and a marker; the left and right collars, the chain adjusters and the bearings all need to stay identified.
steps.title: Wash and prep

steps.instruction: Put the bike on a stand under the engine so both wheels can be lifted clear. Make sure it is stable before pulling on anything.
steps.title: Get the bike on the stand

steps.instruction: Spin each wheel and feel for roughness, then rock it side to side to feel for play. Write down what you find for front and rear.
steps.title: Check the bearings
verification: Front and rear bearing condition noted

steps.instruction: Undo the speed sensor bracket bolt on the left fork leg and lift the sensor away from the wheel without pulling on its lead. Tape it to the fork guard so it hangs clear. Keep magnetic tools away from the sensor and its rotor on the wheel.
steps.title: Unbolt the speed sensor
verification: Sensor hanging free, lead not stretched

steps.instruction: Loosen the four axle pinch bolts at the bottom of both fork legs, then crack the axle nut loose. Do not take anything off yet; the wheel is still holding the forks in line.
steps.title: Loosen the axle
verification: Pinch bolts and axle nut loose

steps.instruction: Hold the wheel, unscrew the axle nut and slide the axle out. Lower the wheel out of the forks and lay it with the disc facing up. Pick up the two collars from the hub and keep them with the axle so they go back on the correct sides.
steps.title: Pull the front wheel
verification: Wheel out, axle and both collars bagged together

steps.instruction: Remove the rear axle nut. Loosen the chain adjuster locknuts and turn the adjusting bolts in so the wheel can move forward.
steps.title: Loosen the rear axle and adjusters

steps.instruction: Push the wheel forward and lift the chain off the sprocket. Hold the wheel, slide the axle out and lower the wheel out of the swingarm, guiding the disc out of the caliper. Keep both collars and the left and right chain pullers bagged and labeled. Do not press the rear brake pedal while the wheel is out.
steps.title: Pull the rear wheel

steps.instruction: Roll each axle on a flat surface and look for any rocking that shows a bend. Check the collars for wear steps or damage. A bent axle is replaced, not straightened.
steps.title: Check the axles and collars

steps.instruction: Put each wheel on a truing stand with a dial gauge and spin it slowly. Radial and lateral runout must both be no more than 2.0 mm and 2.0 mm. Note the readings. If spokes are loose, tighten them to the spoke torque first and measure again.
steps.title: Check wheel runout
verification: Radial runout at or under 2.0 mm
Lateral runout at or under 2.0 mm

steps.instruction: Clean the outside of the front hub. Lever both seals out with a flat screwdriver, with a folded rag under the blade so you do not mark the hub. These seals are not reused.
steps.title: Pry out the front seals

steps.instruction: Remove both front bearings with a bearing puller (or drive each one out from the other side by shifting the center spacer and tapping around the inner race). Keep the center spacer. Clean the hub bores and look for scoring or cracks.
steps.title: Pull the front bearings

steps.instruction: Press the new left-side bearing in first, then drop the spacer in and press in the right-side bearing. Use a socket that bears only on the outer race and keep the bearing square as it goes in; stop when it seats.
steps.title: Fit the new front bearings

steps.instruction: Grease the lips of two new seals with lithium-soap grease and drive them in with the maker's marks facing out, flush with the hub face. Use a socket that matches the seal outer diameter.
steps.title: Fit the new front seals

steps.instruction: Look over the speed sensor rotor on the hub for cracks or damage and wipe off any iron dust or solvent. Check its rubber dampers are not cracked. Keep magnets away from it.
steps.title: Check the speed sensor rotor

steps.instruction: Clean the rear hub and lever both seals out with a flat screwdriver over a rag, same as the front.
steps.title: Pry out the rear seals

steps.instruction: Remove the circlip on the brake-disc side with circlip pliers, then pull all 3 rear bearings and the center spacer. Clean the bores and check them for scoring or cracks.
steps.title: Pull the rear bearings

steps.instruction: Press the new right-side (brake disc side) bearing in first and fit a new circlip in its groove. Then drop in the spacer and press in the left-side (sprocket side) two bearings. Push only on the outer race and keep each bearing square.
steps.title: Fit the new rear bearings
verification: New circlip fully in its groove
Spacer and left-side two bearings seated

steps.instruction: Grease the lips of two new seals and drive them in with the marks facing out, set about 1.0 mm below the hub face.
steps.title: Fit the new rear seals

steps.instruction: If you removed a disc or the sprocket, refit them now: disc bolts with medium threadlocker at 12 N·m (8.9 lb-ft) (front) and 12 N·m (8.9 lb-ft) (rear), sprocket nuts at 50 N·m (37 lb-ft), all tightened in stages in a criss-cross pattern. Otherwise just check they are tight.
steps.title: Check disc and sprocket fasteners
verification: Disc and sprocket fasteners at spec

steps.instruction: Push a finger through each new bearing and turn it: it should be smooth with no notch. Grease the seal lips again and fit the collars on their correct sides.
steps.title: Spin-test both hubs
verification: Collars fitted on the right sides

steps.instruction: Grease the axle lightly with lithium-soap grease. Fit the collars to the hub on their own sides, lift the wheel into the forks with the disc sliding between the brake pads, and push the axle through from the side it came out.
steps.title: Lift the front wheel into the forks

steps.instruction: Put the speed sensor back on the left leg with its bracket, keeping the lead in its original routing. Tighten the bolt to 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft). Check nothing magnetic or metallic is stuck to the sensor face.
steps.title: Refit the speed sensor

steps.instruction: Fit the axle nut and run it down. Before the final pull, take the bike off the stand or push hard on the bars a few times so the forks settle and slide freely on the axle. Then torque the axle nut to 115 N·m (85 lb-ft).
steps.title: Torque the axle nut

steps.instruction: Tighten the four axle pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft), going back and forth between the two bolts on each leg so the clamp closes evenly.
steps.title: Tighten the axle pinch bolts
verification: All four pinch bolts at 21 N·m (15 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Squeeze the front brake lever several times until it is firm, then spin the wheel. It should turn freely with only light pad drag and stop hard when you pull the lever.
steps.title: Pump up the front brake
verification: Wheel spins freely and brakes properly

steps.instruction: If the caliper was disturbed, confirm its two bolts are at 28 N·m (21 lb-ft).
steps.title: Check the front caliper

steps.instruction: Put the left chain puller on the axle and grease the axle. Lift the wheel into the swingarm with the disc going between the rear pads, push the wheel forward and loop the chain on the sprocket, then push the axle through from the left side. Fit the right puller, washer and axle nut finger tight.
steps.title: Lift the rear wheel in

steps.instruction: With the bike on the stand, set the chain slack to 50.0–60.0 mm by turning both adjusting bolts the same amount so the marks match on each side. Measure and record the slack.
steps.title: Set the chain slack

steps.instruction: Torque the rear axle nut to 135 N·m (100 lb-ft), then tighten both adjuster locknuts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft). Recheck the slack.
steps.title: Torque the rear axle

steps.instruction: Press the rear brake pedal until it is firm. Spin the wheel: it should turn freely and stop hard with the pedal.
steps.title: Pump up the rear brake

steps.instruction: Spin both wheels and check for wobble and noise. Off the stand, push the bike and use both brakes. Recheck the axle nuts after the first ride.
steps.title: Final check

completeness: Takes the front wheel, fork legs, handlebar and both triple clamps off, then either cleans and regreases the steering head bearings or replaces both bearings and races, sets the bearing preload and rebuilds to a ready-to-ride front end; fork internals are not opened.
critical_stop_conditions: Bearing race bore in the head tube scored, cracked or loose on a new race: stop, this is frame repair.
New bearings still notchy after assembly: stop and recheck that both races are fully seated before riding.
Any front-to-back play at the steering head after adjustment: do not ride.
Steering binds after the stem nut is torqued: back the ring nut off slightly and recheck; never ride with tight steering.
Brake hose kinked or stretched while the caliper hangs: inspect it and replace if damaged.
entry_state: Complete bike, cold, on a stand under the engine.
excluded: Frame repair or a damaged head tube bore
exit_state: Steering head bearings regreased or renewed, ring nut preload set, clamps, fork legs, handlebar, fender and front wheel refitted and torqued, steering free of play and binding; ready to ride.

Note the fork leg height in the clamps and your clicker settings before you start.

required_parts.purpose: Only if inspection shows damage or pitting; bearings and races are always replaced as a set
